cases.name: selection preserves dependency and acceptance obligations
cases.scenario: Review the changed-boundary development runner for false-green selections after a Rust, frontend or shared-input change. Evaluate current implementation, not aspirations.
rubric: Unmapped changes block unless explicitly assigned with a reason; shared inputs reach consumers and deleted-source dependencies are considered.
Cheap static checks precede heavy work, and changed inputs invalidate the queued handoff and final verdict.

Test selectors must execute nonignored tests and each selected frontend or diagnostic file must execute at least one passing declared test case; skipped-only runs and file wrappers cannot qualify. Test-case counts are not proof of assertion-call counts or test quality.
Browser/native escalation and full publication gates remain explicit obligations; selected development success cannot authorize a merge.

cases.name: reuse and cancellation cannot turn stale work into proof
cases.scenario: Assess trusted local reuse, process cancellation and cache cleanup. Identify concrete paths to stale success or premature resource release. Do not infer measured speedups from mechanisms.
rubric: Reuse checks source or registered input closure, tool/config/environment identity, artifacts and log integrity, and expires evidence.
Dirty source, CI and explicit fresh execution do not reuse successful local verdicts; source changes during work cannot publish reusable success.
POSIX nested cancellation retains resource ownership through descendant cleanup; platform-specific limitations are disclosed rather than treated as proved.
Automatic cleanup protects recently used verified caches and active builds; explicit cleanup policy and soft budget limits are accurately described.

cases.name: CI acceleration preserves protected checks and coverage identity
cases.scenario: Evaluate workflow optimization for missing checks, skipped-success aggregates and cross-run artifact substitution. Source review is not evidence of hosted execution or enabled branch settings.
rubric: Stable aggregate checks use always() and explicitly require successful dependencies instead of trusting skipped checks.
Merge groups trigger the affected checks and dependency review uses the queued base/head delta.
Shared coverage stays in the same workflow/run/attempt/source/platform identity and validates content before restoring output.
Required desktop platform matrices and full suites remain present; claimed redundant work removal does not remove its owning validation.

cases.name: feedback measurements cannot exaggerate quality or speed
cases.scenario: Assess whether reports distinguish first observed command, first actionable issue, total completion, cache reuse and actual acceptance. Look for unsupported zero-miss, regression-rate or latency-improvement claims.
rubric: Command completion is distinct from successful assertions and from final acceptance; candidateReady remains false for development reports.
Failures, unavailable tools, invalidated source, cancellation, blocked and empty selections are kept distinct; cancellation does not erase an earlier issue.
Missing or invalid timestamps stay unknown, snapshots are replayable, repeated observations deduplicate without collapsing distinct invocations.
Scope/platform/timing origin and cache reuse stay visible; selection audits and small sample quantiles do not prove zero misses or unmeasured speed improvements.
